newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to release Palestinian women prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Israel to release Palestinian women prisoners.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that all female Palestinian prisoners held by Israel would be freed, fulfilling part of a commitment made in an interim peace deal with the PLO.
Only 25 of the nearly 5,000 Palestinian prisoners held by Israel are women, Palestinian activists say.
Israeli media said in a parallel move the government would ask Israeli President Ezer Weizman to consider pardoning Jews "convicted of terrorist acts against Arabs".
The spokesmen of Netanyahu and Weizman were not immediately available to comment on that report.
A cabinet statement issued after the weekly meeting on Friday said: "The prime minister reported to the government ministers that an order was given to free the Palestinian female prisoners."
The cabinet statement made no mention of consideration of release of Jews convicted of attacks on Arabs.

Israel Radio and Israel's army radio said Netanyahu told the cabinet that Weizman would be asked to consider, once the Palestinian women were freed, pardoning Jewish prisoners like Ami Popper who was sentenced to seven life terms for killing seven Palestinian labourers waiting for work in Israel in 1990.

The cabinet statement said that, in line with an agreeement Israel's previous government made, the Palestinian women prisoners would have to sign an undertaking "to obey the law and to refrain from terrorist activities".
It gave no date for the release, however, and Netanyahu's spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.
One Israeli security source told Reuters: "It won't be before Monday...also there could be appeals (against it) to the High Court on Sunday."

Netanyahu is to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday at Erez in the Gaza Strip. Arafat controls self-rule enclaves in the Gaza Strip and West Bank set up under interim peace deals with Israel. Final peace talks have yet to begin.

Netanyahu, who ousted Israel's previous government in elections last May, has said he will honour all commitments signed by that government. The release of female, sick and young prisoners was a commitment made in a deal signed by the previous government in September 1995 with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
Israel released some of the male sick and elderly prisoners but others are still in prison.

Weizman at first refused to pardon some of the women prisoners who were involved in deadly attacks against Israelis. The female prisoners that he did pardon then chose to remain in prison in solidarity with their comrades.
The cabinet statement said the president had now decided to pardon all of the women.

In a deal with the PLO in January under which Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron, also fulfilling an accord signed by the prior government, Netanyahu pledged to carry out the prisoner releases.
Israel redeployed in Hebron in January but Arafat has accused it of foot-dragging on implementing addenda to the Hebron agreement like the prisoner releases.
